correctness.rationale: A nonconstant affine self-map on an unbounded positive set has positive slope. Iteration on a fixed nonzero integral difference forces the rational slope to be a positive integer by unbounded prime-power denominators. The consecutive-ratio limit bounds the displacement m(n)-n, forces an eventual unique fixed shift j with a=rho^j; j>0 gives a diverging positive-weight telescoping sum of the one-step drifts incompatible with a constant intercept. Thus j=0,a=1,b=0. Exact factorial quotient expansions give 1-1/(2n)+O(1/n^2) for fixed-slope binomials and 1-3/(2n)+O(1/n^2) for Fuss–Catalan, so differences tend to minus infinity. Independently checked 669 exact finite rising/negative drift inequalities. Finite checks are not universal proofs.

value.rationale: The result supplies a simple sufficient structural obstruction with a genuine sharp boundary: translated geometric progressions violate divergent drift and possess nontrivial affine endomorphisms. It yields complete symmetry classifications across infinite naturally occurring combinatorial sequences and a reusable tool for other exponential enumerators, not an arbitrary finite fit.

final_claim: An eventually increasing positive integer sequence with consecutive ratio approaching rho>1 and one-step drift u_(n+1)-rho*u_n tending to plus or minus infinity has no real affine value-set self-map except identity or constants. This applies to all fixed-r Fuss–Catalan sequences and binom(mn,ln), m>l>=1, with a shifted geometric boundary counterexample.
limitations: Eventually increasing positive integers; ratio must converge to rho>1, and drift must tend to a signed infinity.
All affine coefficients real; no claim for bounded/oscillatory drift or arbitrary sequences.
residual_risks: An older value-set homothety or exponential-gap rigidity lemma might exist under unindexed terminology.
The exact theorem is a sufficient condition, not a necessary condition for all exponentially growing sequences.
